title: Fall Garden · Zone 7b
disclaimer: General public horticulture guidance for USDA zone 7b (central Maryland). Not a soil test, pest diagnosis, or site-specific landscape prescription. Adjust for your microclimate, drainage, and HOA rules.

months.label: October
months.focus: Plant garlic & spring bulbs · start leaf mulch · cut spent annuals

tasks.label: Plant hardneck garlic cloves 2–3" deep, pointy end up
Begin planting tulips, daffodils, alliums (soil still workable)
Sow winter rye or crimson clover in empty beds
Cut back diseased foliage; leave healthy seedheads for birds
Start shredding leaves for mulch (keep some whole for habitat)
Deep-water newly planted bulbs & garlic if dry

months.label: November
months.focus: Finish garlic · bulbs by Thanksgiving · mulch beds · tidy perennials

tasks.label: Finish garlic planting before ground freezes hard
Complete spring bulb planting by Thanksgiving if soil allows
Apply 2–3" shredded-leaf mulch after soil cools
Cut back peony foliage to soil line; leave ornamental grasses standing
Clean & oil tools; drain hoses before hard freeze
Add leaf pile / compost turn for spring soil

plantNow.name: Hardneck garlic
plantNow.how: Separate cloves from bulbs the day you plant. Space 4–6" apart in rows 12" apart. Pointy tip up, 2–3" deep. Mulch lightly after planting.
plantNow.why: Needs winter chill for good bulb formation. Millersville 7b winters usually deliver it.

plantNow.name: Winter rye (cover crop)
plantNow.how: Broadcast in empty veg beds, rake lightly, keep moist until established. Terminate in spring before seed set.
plantNow.why: Holds soil, adds organic matter, suppresses winter weeds.

plantNow.name: Crimson clover
plantNow.how: Sow on bare soil; inoculate if soil is new. Pretty spring bloom; cut before seed if you want fewer volunteers.
plantNow.why: Nitrogen-fixing cover that looks good and feeds soil.

plantNow.name: Overwinter spinach (protected)
plantNow.how: Sow thick; cover with floating row cover or cold frame. Harvest small leaves through mild spells.
plantNow.why: Zone 7b can overwinter hardy greens with protection.

plantNow.name: Shallot sets
plantNow.how: Plant like garlic — tips just below soil, mulch after first hard frost.
plantNow.why: Same chill logic as garlic; harvest next summer.

bulbs.name: Daffodils
bulbs.note: Reliable in MD; deer usually leave them alone. Plant by Thanksgiving.

bulbs.name: Tulips
bulbs.note: Treat as annuals if squirrels dig; chicken wire over bed helps. Chill already done in fridge if pre-chilled packs.

bulbs.name: Alliums
bulbs.note: Architectural spring/early summer bloom; plant larger bulbs deeper.

bulbs.name: Crocus
bulbs.note: Early color; squirrels love them — plant in pots or under wire.

bulbs.name: Hyacinths
bulbs.note: Fragrant; gloves recommended — bulbs can irritate skin.

leafCare.title: Shredded leaf mulch
leafCare.body: Run a mower over dry leaves (or use a shredder). 2–3" around perennials and under shrubs after soil cools. Keeps moisture, feeds microbes, suppresses weeds.

leafCare.title: Lawn leaf layer
leafCare.body: A thin shredded layer can stay on turf. Thick wet mats smother grass — bag or move those to beds/compost.

leafCare.title: Leave some leaves
leafCare.body: A corner pile or under shrubs shelters overwintering insects and pollinators. Balance tidy curb appeal with one wild edge.

leafCare.title: Diseased foliage out
leafCare.body: Bag black-spot roses, mildewed squash vines, etc. — do not compost into unfinished piles. Trash or hot-compost only.

leafCare.title: Gutters & drains
leafCare.body: Millersville fall storms + leaf dams = basement risk. Clear gutters and downspouts while you're leaf-raking.

cutBack.label: Peony foliage to soil line after frost
Daylily spent scapes; foliage after frost kill
Do not hard-prune oakleaf/mophead hydrangeas now
